name: Engine cooling fan impeller, WE43 magnesium concept F1 redesigned from the Turbo rotor rebuild
description: Improved variant of the 993 Turbo cooling fan rotor, drawn from the repository's visual rebuild of the original. It keeps the rebuild's 245 mm envelope, its 165 mm cup 56 mm deep that wraps the alternator end, the cup's twelve windows, three bolt holes and bore, eleven blades and no shroud. It replaces the rebuild's constant-pitch cambered plates with twisted airfoil blades designed from velocity triangles, and moves to LPBF WE43 magnesium. A one-dimensional blade-element model with radial equilibrium, on a duty inferred from the rebuild, estimates about 2 % more air than the rebuild rotor on the same shaft power, and about 9 % with a matched stator. These are model estimates on visual hypotheses, not measurements and not a comparison with the Porsche part.

classification.intended_use: F1 design study: airfoil blades inside the original rotor's envelope, one-dimensional fan-curve comparison with the rebuild rotor on a duty inferred from it, lighter-alloy comparison; no manufacture, rotation, installation or start-up authorized

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Magnesium is anodic to the steel bolts, the bearing hub and the aluminium housing: coating, insulating washers and inserts at the bolts are required.

known_limits: The rebuild of the original rotor is a visual reconstruction: blade and window counts are observed, the 48 degree pitch, chords, cup depth and walls are hypotheses.
The duty is inferred from the rebuild (its best-efficiency point at 10,000 fan rpm in a bellmouth housing: 2.34 m3/s at 2,155 Pa); no 993 fan map, pulley ratio or engine resistance is measured.
The flow gains come from a one-dimensional blade-element model with simple radial equilibrium, not CFD or a rig test; the alternator air through the cup windows is not modelled.

On the same shaft power F1 moves about 2 % more air than the rebuild rotor and keeps its stall margin; the same-speed gain ranges from -5 % to +12 % when the rebuild's pitch is varied from 53 to 43 degrees.

Both rotors lose more to the 3.5 mm tip gap and to exit swirl than to blade profile; the matched stator (about +9 % at equal power) and a housing land over the tips are the larger levers, and belong to a future housing.
WE43 data are single-laboratory room-temperature coupons plus generic values; no hot, HCF or notched allowable.
The fully constrained thermal screen fails for WE43; the bolted joint to the bearing hub needs inserts or creep-rated washers.
The open-blade first mode (about 1,350 Hz) is 35 % above the six-spoke order by a beam estimate; an FE Campbell diagram is required.
An earlier F1 revision (120 mm hub, shroud, 248 mm) was a generic fan that did not keep the original cup or alternator space; it is superseded.
The flat-fan sizing study F2 is a separate shrouded rotor family on F0-scaled duties; its findings do not describe this upright rotor.
